theory.intro: A partial cylinder is a cylinder with something removed: a missing lid, open ends, or only half or a quarter kept. The closed-cylinder formula $A = 2\pi r^{2} + 2\pi rh$ still guides you, but count only the faces present and add any flat face the cut exposes.
facts: Each **full circular end** is $\pi r^{2}$; the whole **curved surface** of a full cylinder is $2\pi rh$.
Always ask: which ends are present, how much curved surface remains, and does the cut expose a **new flat face**?
Keep the working exact and round only on the last line; a rounded decimal is written with $\approx$.
steps: Identify which surfaces the solid actually has.
Write the area of each surface that is present.
Add the surface areas, then round or leave in terms of $\pi$ as asked.

foundation.solution_text:
An open-top cylinder has one circular base and the curved surface, but no lid.
$A = \pi r^{2} + 2\pi rh$
$= \pi(5)^{2} + 2\pi(5)(12)$
$= 25\pi + 120\pi$
$= 145\pi$
$= 455.5309\ldots$
$\approx 455.5\text{ cm}^{2}$

A pipe open at both ends has only its curved surface.
$A = 2\pi rh$
$= 2\pi(4)(20)$
$= 160\pi$
$= 502.6548\ldots$
$\approx 502.7\text{ cm}^{2}$

A closed half-cylinder has two semicircular ends ($\pi r^{2}$ altogether), half the curved surface ($\pi rh$), and a flat rectangular top ($2r \times h$).
$A = \pi r^{2} + \pi rh + 2rh$
$= \pi(6)^{2} + \pi(6)(10) + 2(6)(10)$
$= 36\pi + 60\pi + 120$
$= 96\pi + 120$
$= 421.6106\ldots$
$\approx 421.61\text{ cm}^{2}$

An open-top half-cylinder has two semicircular ends ($\pi r^{2}$ altogether) and half the curved surface ($\pi rh$), but no flat top.
$A = \pi r^{2} + \pi rh$
$= \pi(3)^{2} + \pi(3)(8)$
$= 9\pi + 24\pi$
$= 33\pi$
$= 103.6725\ldots$
$\approx 103.67\text{ cm}^{2}$

$r = \frac{10}{2} = 5$
An open-top cylinder has one circular base and the curved surface, but no lid.
$A = \pi r^{2} + 2\pi rh$
$= \pi(5)^{2} + 2\pi(5)(9)$
$= 25\pi + 90\pi$
$= 115\pi$
$= 361.2831\ldots$
$\approx 361.3\text{ cm}^{2}$

$r = \frac{14}{2} = 7$
A pipe open at both ends has only its curved surface.
$A = 2\pi rh$
$= 2\pi(7)(30)$
$= 420\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$

A closed half-cylinder has two semicircular ends ($\pi r^{2}$ altogether), half the curved surface ($\pi rh$), and a flat rectangular top ($2r \times h$).
$A = \pi r^{2} + \pi rh + 2rh$
$= \pi(4)^{2} + \pi(4)(9) + 2(4)(9)$
$= 16\pi + 36\pi + 72$
$= 52\pi + 72\text{ cm}^{2}$

An open-top half-cylinder has two semicircular ends ($\pi r^{2}$ altogether) and half the curved surface ($\pi rh$), but no flat top.
$A = \pi r^{2} + \pi rh$
$= \pi(2.5)^{2} + \pi(2.5)(12)$
$= 6.25\pi + 30\pi$
$= 36.25\pi$
$= 113.8848\ldots$
$\approx 113.88\text{ cm}^{2}$

development.solution_text:
A gutter open along the top and at both ends has only its curved surface, which is half a full cylinder's.
$A = \pi rh$
$= \pi(5)(120)$
$= 600\pi$
$= 1884.9556\ldots$
$\approx 1885.0\text{ cm}^{2}$

A closed quarter-cylinder has two quarter-circle ends ($\tfrac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}$ altogether), a quarter of the curved surface ($\tfrac{1}{2}\pi rh$), and two flat rectangular faces ($2rh$).
$A = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2} + \frac{1}{2}\pi rh + 2rh$
$= \frac{1}{2}\pi(8)^{2} + \frac{1}{2}\pi(8)(15) + 2(8)(15)$
$= 32\pi + 60\pi + 240$
$= 92\pi + 240$
$= 529.0265\ldots$
$\approx 529.03\text{ cm}^{2}$

development.question_text: A straight steel pipe is open at both ends. It has a diameter of $40$ cm and a length of $300$ cm. Find the area of steel used to make it, correct to the nearest square centimetre.
development.solution_text:
$r = \frac{40}{2} = 20$
A pipe open at both ends has only its curved surface.
$A = 2\pi rh$
$= 2\pi(20)(300)$
$= 12000\pi$
$= 37699.1118\ldots$
$\approx 37699\text{ cm}^{2}$

development.question_text: An open-top cylindrical bucket has a radius of $15$ cm and a height of $30$ cm. The bucket has a base but no lid. Find the area of metal used to make it, correct to the nearest square centimetre.
development.solution_text:
An open-top cylinder has one circular base and the curved surface, but no lid.
$A = \pi r^{2} + 2\pi rh$
$= \pi(15)^{2} + 2\pi(15)(30)$
$= 225\pi + 900\pi$
$= 1125\pi$
$= 3534.2917\ldots$
$\approx 3534\text{ cm}^{2}$

development.question_text: A closed half-cylinder and an open-top half-cylinder trough both have radius $4$ cm and length $10$ cm. Find both surface areas, correct to $2$ decimal places, and state what the difference between them represents.
development.solution_text:
Closed half-cylinder: $A = \pi r^{2} + \pi rh + 2rh$
$= 16\pi + 40\pi + 80$
$= 56\pi + 80$
$= 255.9292\ldots \approx 255.93\text{ cm}^{2}$
Open-top trough: $A = \pi r^{2} + \pi rh$
$= 16\pi + 40\pi$
$= 56\pi$
$= 175.9292\ldots \approx 175.93\text{ cm}^{2}$
The difference is $2rh = 2(4)(10) = 80$ cm², which is exactly the flat rectangular top that the open trough is missing.

development.question_text: A water trough for animals is a half-cylinder that is open along the top. Its radius is $0.4$ m and its length is $1.5$ m. The inside curved surface and the two semicircular ends are to be sealed with waterproof coating. Find the area to be coated, correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
An open-top half-cylinder has two semicircular ends ($\pi r^{2}$ altogether) and half the curved surface ($\pi rh$).
$A = \pi r^{2} + \pi rh$
$= \pi(0.4)^{2} + \pi(0.4)(1.5)$
$= 0.16\pi + 0.6\pi$
$= 0.76\pi$
$= 2.3876\ldots$
$\approx 2.39\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.question_text: An open-top cylinder (a base but no lid) has a radius of $5$ cm. The total of its base and curved surface is $175\pi$ cm². Find the height of the cylinder.
A pipe is open at both ends and has a radius of $5$ cm. Its surface area is $300\pi$ cm². Find the length of the pipe.
mastery.solution_text:
A pipe open at both ends has only its curved surface.
$2\pi rh = 300\pi$
$2\pi(5)h = 300\pi$
$10\pi h = 300\pi$
$h = 30\text{ cm}$

mastery.question_text: A skateboarding half-pipe is a half-cylinder that is open along the top and at both ends, so only its curved inside surface is skated. Its radius is $3$ m and its length is $12$ m. This curved surface is to be resurfaced, and one tin of surfacing covers $8$ m². How many whole tins are needed?
mastery.solution_text:
A half-pipe open along the top and at both ends has only its curved surface, half a full cylinder's.
$A = \pi rh$
$= \pi(3)(12)$
$= 36\pi$
$= 113.0973\ldots\text{ m}^{2}$
$113.0973\ldots \div 8 = 14.137\ldots$
$15$ tins are needed.
